topic: Coil internals: request pipeline, caches & decoding

questions.question: For a network image that is not yet cached anywhere, in what order does Coil work through its pipeline?
options: Check the disk cache, decode, then check the memory cache
Fetch from network, write to memory cache, then decode on the main thread
Check the memory cache, fetch the source (disk cache or network), decode, then store the result in the memory cache
Decode, then check the memory cache, then fetch
questions.explanation: Coil first looks for a ready decoded image in the memory cache, which is the cheapest hit. On a miss it fetches the source data, from the disk cache or the network, decodes it off the main thread, and stores the decoded image in memory for later requests.

questions.question: When an `ImageView` that Coil is loading into gets a new request, or is detached, Coil cancels the old in-flight request for that view.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Coil tracks the current request per view target and disposes the previous one when a new one starts or the view goes away. This is what prevents recycled list items from flashing the wrong image.

questions.question: What does Coil's disk cache store for a network image?
options: Only the HTTP headers, used to revalidate the image
The decoded bitmap, so no decoding is needed next time
A downsampled copy at the size of the last request
The encoded source bytes as downloaded, which still need decoding
questions.explanation: The disk cache holds the fetched source data, so a disk hit skips the network but still needs decoding at the size the new request asks for. Decoded bitmaps live only in the memory cache, which is why the two caches complement each other.

questions.question: A feed of thumbnails uses `size(Size.ORIGINAL)` on every request, and memory spikes while scrolling. Why?
options: `Size.ORIGINAL` forces software bitmaps
`Size.ORIGINAL` decodes each image at its full pixel dimensions instead of the size it is shown at
`Size.ORIGINAL` turns off the memory cache
`Size.ORIGINAL` downloads the image twice
questions.explanation: Coil normally resolves the target size from the view or layout constraints and downsamples during decode. Asking for the original size skips that, so a 4000 px photo in a 100 dp cell costs tens of megabytes. Caching and the download itself are unaffected.

questions.question: You add a custom Coil `Interceptor` to an ImageLoader. Which is true about it?
options: It runs only after the image is decoded, so it can only change the bitmap
It runs only on memory cache misses
It runs before Coil's own engine, so it can rewrite the request (e.g. add a width to the URL) or return a result itself
It replaces the network layer and must download the bytes itself
questions.explanation: Coil interceptors wrap the request execution, and the engine that checks the memory cache, fetches and decodes runs at the end of the chain. So an interceptor can change the request before any cache lookup or short-circuit with its own result. Transformations, not interceptors, are the usual tool for changing the bitmap.

questions.question: Which of these result in a different memory cache entry for the same URL? Select all that apply.
options: Giving the requests different custom `memoryCacheKey` values
Using a different crossfade duration
Applying a circle-crop transformation versus no transformation
Using a different placeholder drawable
questions.explanation: The memory cache key is built from the data and things that change the decoded output, such as transformations, or set explicitly with `memoryCacheKey`. Placeholders and crossfade only affect how the result is shown, so they do not change which cached image is reused.

questions.question: On Android, Coil may decode images as hardware bitmaps by default, so you should disable hardware bitmaps for a request whose result you need to read pixels from, for example with Palette.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Coil allows hardware bitmaps by default where the platform supports them because they save memory and upload time. Their pixels cannot be read on the CPU, so set `allowHardware(false)` on requests whose bitmap you will inspect.

questions.question: Each screen builds its own `ImageLoader` with `ImageLoader.Builder(context).build()`. What is the main consequence?
options: Each loader has its own memory cache and resources, so memory is duplicated and screens do not share cache hits
All loaders share one memory cache automatically, so there is no impact
Images stop loading after the second screen because only one loader is allowed
Disk caching is disabled for every loader except the first
questions.explanation: Each ImageLoader owns its memory cache and other machinery, so several of them hold separate copies of hot images and cannot reuse each other's decoded results. Coil is designed around a single shared loader, typically provided through the singleton or DI, with `newBuilder()` for variants that share resources.

questions.question: A list shows an image as a small thumbnail, then a detail screen shows the same URL full-screen. Which statements describe Coil's behavior? Select all that apply.
options: The small thumbnail in memory is upscaled and reused for the full-screen request
The thumbnail request decodes with subsampling, so it uses far less memory than the full image
The disk cache stores the thumbnail-sized version, so the detail screen must re-download
A larger decoded image already in the memory cache can satisfy a later, smaller request
questions.explanation: Coil downsamples during decode to the requested size, and when checking the memory cache it accepts a cached image that is large enough. A smaller cached image is not good enough for a bigger request, so Coil decodes again, usually from the disk cache, which holds the original bytes rather than a resized copy.

questions.question: You want `AsyncImage(model = AvatarId("42"))` to work, where an `AvatarId` resolves to a normal HTTPS URL. Which Coil extension point fits best?
options: A custom `Decoder` that turns `AvatarId` into a bitmap
A `Transformation` that replaces the request data
A custom `Fetcher` that downloads the bytes for `AvatarId` itself
A `Mapper` that converts `AvatarId` into its URL, so the standard network fetcher and caches handle the rest
questions.explanation: A Mapper converts your model type into a type Coil already knows, so you keep the built-in network fetching, disk caching and decoding. A Fetcher is for a genuinely new data source, a Decoder for a new image format, and Transformations work on the decoded image, not the request.
